subject.title: fix(config): restore redacted array values by item identity

question: When an edited config array reuses the visible `id` of a removed original row while retaining a redaction placeholder, should OpenClaw reject the save or deliberately restore the removed row’s stored value?
rationale: The submitted payload contains no row-continuity marker beyond `id`, so source code cannot safely infer whether reuse means a retained logical row or a newly created one that must not inherit prior credentials.

options.title: Reject ambiguous ID reuse
options.body: Fail the save when an ID-reused row still contains a redaction placeholder, requiring the user to enter an explicit replacement value.

options.title: Define ID reuse as adoption
options.body: Document and test that reusing an ID intentionally adopts the removed row’s saved redacted values, including credential-routing consequences.

recommendation.title: Reject ambiguous ID reuse
recommendation.body: Fail the save when an ID-reused row still contains a redaction placeholder, requiring the user to enter an explicit replacement value.

likelyOwner.reason: The current candidate implementation and its explicit out-of-scope note identify the unresolved contract boundary.
